examples.label: Positive
examples.description: The code checks that a ≥ 0 in the division point, but it does not prevent a == 0. Division by 0 can still occur, so a divide‑by‑zero error must be reported.

examples.label: Negative
examples.description: The check z ≤ 0 prevents z from ever being 0, so no divide‑by‑zero error can occur on x / z.

examples.label: Negative
examples.description: Here, d is populated from a struct member and never explicitly assigned or bounded by a check inside the given function. Without any checks or constants, we cannot determine whether d could be zero—so by our conservative policy, this is classified as safe.
